events.cmeNote: CME observed to the E in STEREO A COR2 and SE in GOES CCOR-1, not yet in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a DSN gap. The source is a filament eruption spanning approximately ~S05E20 to ~N05E13, centered ~N03E18, and an associated C4.7 flare peaking at 2026-08-25T12:58Z observed in SDO AIA 131; nearby but not associated with AR 14513. Observed as the filament ejecta and brightening in SDO AIA 304 and field line movement, dimming, and brief post-eruptive arcade in SDO AIA 171/193. Also seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 as the filament ejecta at 2026-08-25T12:45Z over its east limb. Significantly overlaps with prior CME: 2026-08-25T10:38Z from AR 14513. This event is preliminarily closed out as arriving at L1 at 2026-08-28T08:30Z. The arrival is characterized by an enhancement in magnetic field components with B_total increasing from 2nT to 13nT, an increase in solar wind speed from approximately 250 km/s to 290 km/s from 2026-08-28T03:00Z to 13:35Z. An additional increase in solar wind speed up to 380 km/s and an increase in temperature is observed at 2026-08-28T13:35Z.

## Summary:

Update on CMEs with IDs 2026-08-25T12:53:00-CME-001 and 2026-08-25T10:38:00-CME-001 (see previous notification 20260825-AL-005).  Based on preliminary analysis by the Moon to Mars Space Weather Analysis Office and heliospheric modeling carried out at NASA Community Coordinated Modeling Center, it is estimated that the CMEs may affect Europa Clipper, Juice, OSIRIS-APEX, and Solar Orbiter.  The leading edge of the CMEs will reach Europa Clipper at 2026-08-28T08:49Z, Juice at 2026-08-29T00:19Z, OSIRIS-APEX at 2026-08-28T21:01Z, and Solar Orbiter at 2026-08-26T07:43Z (plus minus 7 hours). 

The simulation also indicates that the CMEs may impact NASA missions near Earth. Simulations indicate that the leading edge of the CMEs will reach NASA missions near Earth at about 2026-08-28T09:25Z (plus minus 7 hours). The roughly estimated expected range of the maximum Kp index is 4-6 (below minor to moderate).

events.cmeNote: CME observed to the N/NW in SOHO LASCO C2 and not yet in LASCO C3 before a DSN gap begins at 2026-08-08T05:00Z. The CME is visible to the N/NW in GOES CCOR-1 but heavily obscured by the pylon. The CME is best seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The source is a filament eruption on the north central disk; the full eruption spans approximately N28E35 to N08W00, centered ~N20E10 in SDO AIA 193. The eruption is observed as filament ejecta and double ribbon flare in SDO AIA 304 first lifting around 2026-08-08T00:48Z and fully erupting at 2026-08-08T02:10Z. The CME is also seen as a prominence on the NE limb of STEREO A EUVI 195/304. Dimming, field line movement, and post eruptive arcades are observed in SDO AIA 171/193. | Characterized by a jump in B_total from 5.6nT to 9.8nT, with B_z initially flipping northward and southward +-5nT. Alongside a jump in speed from ~350km/s to ~400km/s, density from 3.07p/cc to 7.09p/cc, and temperature from 45.3kK to 167kK.

## Summary:

Ensemble modeling update on CME with ID 2026-08-08T03:23:00-CME-001 (see previous notification 20260808-AL-007). Based on heliospheric ensemble modeling carried out at the Moon to Mars Space Weather Analysis Office, it is estimated that the CME may impact NASA missions near Earth. Out of 36 ensemble members (see notes section), 35 (97%) indicate impact at NASA missions near Earth. Ensemble simulations indicate that the leading edge of the CME will reach NASA missions near Earth between about 2026-08-11T00:19Z and 2026-08-11T23:25Z (average arrival 2026-08-11T10:32Z). The ensemble-based forecast indicates that there is a 89% chance for the maximum Kp index to be in the 3-5 range (below minor to minor).

https://iswa.gsfc.nasa.gov/ENSEMBLE/2026-08-08_ncmes1_sims36_M2M-SWAO097/20260808_032300_ncmes1_sims36_M2M-SWAO097_anim_tim-den.gif

## Notes:
The CME event with ID 2026-08-08T03:23:00-CME-001 is also predicted to impact Juice at 2026-08-12T09:47Z, OSIRIS-APEX at 2026-08-12T13:55Z, Parker Solar Probe at 2026-08-10T02:28Z, Europa Clipper at 2026-08-12T12:00Z (glancing blow) and STEREO A at 2026-08-11T20:00Z (glancing blow) (plus minus 7 hours) based on previous heliospheric modeling (see notification 20260808-AL-007).

Ensemble CME modeling at M2M is performed by building sets of initial CME parameters and carrying out separate simulations for each set. This approach allows a mapping of initial CME parameter uncertainties into a statistical characterization of CME arrival times and impact at locations of interest.

Description of links: For each location, the first link shows the WSA-ENLIL+Cone model animation for the median CME input parameters, the second link shows the probabilistic distribution of predicted arrival times histogram, and the third link shows a stack plot of the WSA-ENLIL+Cone modeled magnetic field, velocity, density, and temperature for all ensemble members. For missions near Earth, a histogram of the probabilistic Kp forecast is also provided.

events.cmeNote: CME observed as a NE halo in STEREO A COR2, and a NW halo in GOES CCOR-1 partially blocked by the pylon. SOHO LASCO C2/C3 not available in real-time due to a downlink gap. The source is associated with an M1.9 flare from AR 14492 peaking at 2026-07-30T17:00Z, observed in SDO AIA 131. This eruption is also observed as filament ejecta in SDO AIA 304 first lifting as early as 2026-07-30T15:18Z, more eruptively after 2026-07-15:43Z. SDO AIA 171/193 observe brightening, dimming, field line movement, EUV wave, and post-eruptive arcades. | Arrival: Characterized by a sharp increase in magnetic field components with Btotal jumping from ~4.4nT to ~14.3 at 2026-08-02T11:28Z, reaching a maximum B_total of 21.5nT at 2026-08-02T14:56Z and maximum southward B_z of -17.41nT at 2026-08-02T15:02Z. There is a corresponding sharp increase in speed observed from ~290 km/s to ~360 km/s, reaching a maximum speed ~430 km/s. Temperature also increases from ~34,000 K to ~313,000 K further reaching ~479.6k K, with density increasing from ~3 p/cc to ~37 p/cc. This signature is associated with the arrival of CME: 2026-07-30T16:53Z.

## Summary:

Update on CME with ID 2026-07-30T16:53:00-CME-001 (see previous notification 20260730-AL-004). Based on preliminary analysis by the Moon to Mars Space Weather Analysis Office and heliospheric modeling carried out at NASA Community Coordinated Modeling Center, it is estimated that this CME may affect BepiColombo, Juice, Parker Solar Probe, STEREO A, Mars (glancing blow), OSIRIS-APEX (glancing blow), and Psyche (glancing blow). The leading edge of the CME will reach BepiColombo at 2026-07-31T07:01Z, Juice at 2026-08-02T12:57Z, Parker Solar Probe at 2026-08-01T00:19Z, and STEREO A at 2026-08-01T17:02Z. The flank may reach Mars at 2026-08-03T20:00Z, OSIRIS-APEX at 2026-08-03T04:00Z, and Psyche at 2026-08-04T00:00Z (plus minus 7 hours). 

The simulation also indicates that the CME may impact NASA missions near Earth. Simulations indicate that the leading edge of the CME will reach NASA missions near Earth at about 2026-08-01T22:52Z (plus minus 7 hours). The roughly estimated expected range of the maximum Kp index is 4-6 (below minor to moderate).

produced a long-duration M1.9/Sf (R1-Minor) flare at 30/1700 UTC.
Coinciding with the flare was an approximately eight-degree-long
filament eruption, centered near N20W67. Additionally, two Type II radio
sweeps were observed: the first at 30/1627 UTC (est.853 km/s), and the
second at 30/1645 UTC (est. 1,681 km/s). Other radio events included a
Type IV sweep at 30/1631 UTC, and a 17-minute-long Tenflare (190 sfu)
that peaked at 30/1643 UTC.

A partial-halo CME was observed in GOES CCOR2 coronagraph imagery,
beginning at 30/1715 UTC, as well as a full-halo signature in STEREO
COR2 coronagraph imagery at 30/1653 UTC. Results from WSA-Enlil runs
suggested possible arrival at Earth early on 02 Aug.

Regions 4500 (N18E35, Dao/beta), 4498 (N14E29, Dai/beta0gamma), 4499
(N05W02, Dao/beta-gamma-delta), and 4496 (N05W31, Cao/beta) all
exhibited growth over the past 24 hours. Only minor changes were
observed in the remaining numbered active regions on the visible disk.

.Forecast...
Solar activity is expected to be low with a chance for M-class flares
(R1-R2, Minor-Moderate) over 31 Jul - 02 August.

Energetic Particle

.24 hr Summary...
The greater than 2 MeV electron flux was at normal to moderate levels.
The greater than 10 MeV proton flux reached S1 (Minor) storm levels at

UTC. Additionally, the greater than 100 MeV proton flux briefly exceeded
1 pfu at 30/1825 UTC. All proton flux enhancements were likely
associated with the M1.9/Sf flare from Region 4492 mentioned above.

.Forecast...
The greater than 2 MeV electron flux is likely to remain at normal to
moderate levels over the next three days. There remains a chance for the
greater than 10 MeV proton flux to reach S1 levels over 31 Jul and 01
Aug.

strength was below 5 nT. Solar wind speeds were mostly between ~300-330
km/s. Phi angle was predominantly oriented in the positive solar sector.

31 July as the CMEs from 26 and 27 July may yet graze the Earth. An

additional CME that left the Sun late on 27 July combined with weak CH
HSS influence. A more pronounced enhancement in solar wind parameters is
likely early on 02 Aug as the CME that left the Sun on 30 Jul passes by
Earth.

# Prepared by the U.S. Dept. of Commerce, NOAA, Space Weather Prediction Center
#
Solar Activity

.24 hr Summary...
Solar activity remained at low levels, with the largest flare of the
reporting period being a C6.0/1f flare at 10/1459 UTC from Region 4485
(S10W68, Dac/beta-gamma). An associated CME was first observed in LASCO
C2 coronagraph imagery at approximately 10/1512 UTC. Modelling and
analysis of this event indicated the bulk of the material should pass
ahead of Earth. This region continues to show new flux emergence, with
notable development in its intermediate spot area. The remaining regions
were stable or showing signs of decay.

From around 10/1310-1445 UTC, an approximately seven degree long
filament, centered near N05E65, was seen lifting off from the Sun in
GONG H-Alpha imagery. Due to the location near the East limb, and its
trajectory, no Earth-directed component is expected.

.Forecast...
Solar activity is expected to remain at low levels, with a slight chance
for M-class (R1-R2/Minor-Moderate) flares through 13 Jul, mainly due to
the complexity and flare potential of Region 4485.

Energetic Particle

.24 hr Summary...
The greater than 2 MeV electron flux at geosynchronous orbit reached
high levels, with a peak flux of 2,028 pfu observed at 10/1545 UTC. The
greater than 10 MeV proton flux remained at background levels.

.Forecast...
The greater than 2 MeV electron flux is expected to reach high levels
over 11-13 Jul under high-speed stream influences. The greater than 10
MeV proton flux is anticipated to remain at background levels through 13
July.

Solar Wind

.24 hr Summary...
Solar wind parameters reflected the ongoing and waning influence of a
negative polarity coronal hole high-speed stream. Solar wind speeds
decreased from ~650 km/s to approximately 500 km/s by the end of the
period. Total field strength was predominantly averaged 5 nT, with a
variable Bz component that ranged +/- 5 nT. The phi angle remained
predominantly in the negative sector.

.Forecast...
Elevated but diminishing solar wind parameters are expected on 11 Jul as
effects from the high-speed stream are anticipated to continue weakening
throughout the day. Another enhancement is anticipated mid to late in
the UTC day on 12 Jul due to possible glancing influences from a CME
that departed the Sun on 09 Jul. By 13 Jul, the elevated conditions are
expected to begin tapering off, returning the environment back to near
background levels.

Geospace

.24 hr Summary...
The geomagnetic field was quiet to unsettled under the weakening
influence of the high-speed stream.

.Forecast...
Persistent -CH HSS influences are likely to keep the geomagnetic field 
under slightly elevated conditions, with mostly quiet to unsettled
levels, and a chance for isolated active periods on 11 Jul. By around
midday on 12 Jul, active conditions are anticipated, with isolated
periods of G1 (Minor) storming conditions likely, due to the possible
glancing impacts of the 09 Jul CME, though confidence on timing and
magnitude remains low. Conditions should begin to taper down by 13 Jul
as the CME completes its transit past Earth, bringing levels down to
mostly quiet for the remainder of the day.

events.cmeNote: CME first seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-06-26T21:12Z. It is also seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SE in STEREO A COR2. The most likely source candidate for this CME is a region of southward directed dimming best seen in SDO AIA 195 starting around 2026-06-26T17:34Z centered around S30E05. There is also some field line movement likely associated with this dimming over the S limb best seen in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-06-26T20:06Z and in GOES SUVI 284 beginning around 2026-06-26T19:49Z. A much less likely source candidate for this CME is associated with a C2.4 class flare from AR 14475 (S09W04) that peaked at 2026-06-26T20:21Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131, but the eruption followed by some post eruptive arcades is best seen in SDO AIA 304 and SDO AIA 195. Arrival characterized by an amplification of magnetic field components with Btotal increasing from 4nT at 2026-06-30T11:01Z to 10nT at 2026-06-30T11:22Z. A subsequent increase in solar wind speed is observed from ~340 km/s at 2026-06-30T11:01Z to 437 km/s at 2026-06-30T11:07Z. Increases in temperature, from ~65,000 K to ~430,000 K, and density, from ~1 p/cc to 11 p/cc, are also observed at 2026-06-30T11:01Z.

Update on CME with ID 2026-06-26T21:12:00-CME-001.  Based on preliminary analysis by the Moon to Mars Space Weather Analysis Office and heliospheric modeling carried out at NASA Community Coordinated Modeling Center, it is estimated that this CME may affect BepiColombo, Europa Clipper (glancing blow), Juice (glancing blow), OSIRIS-APEX (glancing blow), and Parker Solar Probe (glancing blow). The flank of the CME may reach BepiColombo at 2026-06-28T12:09Z, Juice at 2026-07-01T18:00Z, OSIRIS-APEX at 2026-07-01T12:00Z, and Parker Solar Probe at 2026-06-28T16:00Z (plus minus 7 hours), while the leading edge may reach Europa Clipper at 2026-07-01T14:00Z. 

The simulation also indicates that the CME may impact NASA missions near Earth. Simulations indicate that the leading edge of the CME will reach NASA missions near Earth at about 2026-06-30T11:01Z (plus minus 7 hours). The roughly estimated expected range of the maximum Kp index is 3-5 (below minor to minor).

This flare can be seen in SDO AIA 131 along with a wide region of dimming, field line opening and an EUV wave seen in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284. | Arrival note: Arrival signature characterized by a sharp jump in B_total from ~5 nT to ~8 nT accompanied by a sharp increase in solar wind speed form ~550 km/s to ~630 km/s as well as an increase in temperature from ~135k K to ~364k K and an increase in density from ~5 p/cc to ~14 p/cc. Starting around 2026-06-13T13:44Z, the magnetic field components become more stable with time until about 20:00Z, potentially indicating the presence of one or more passing flux ropes. This event is most likely associated with the arrival of CME: 2026-06-11T00:36Z. Two other CMEs, CME: 2026-06-09T16:36Z and CME: 2026-06-09T21:36Z, were also anticipated to provide very weak glancing blows within this timeframe, but have more likely missed.

The CME was directed primarily towards the northeast from Earth's perspective and was associated with a long-duration C6.7 flare (SIDC Flare 7923), peaking at 00:02 UTC on June 11, produced by SIDC Sunspot Group 870 (NOAA Active Region 4465), as well as with Type II and Type IV radio emissions detected at 00:13 UTC and 00:28 UTC on June 11, respectively. Associated coronal dimming and an EUV wave were also observed in SDO/AIA data. The bulk of the ejecta is expected to miss Earth, although a glancing blow could be possible on June 13.

The eruption is best seen in SDO AIA 193 as moving field lines and a large area of dimming directed toward the south. The eruption is also accompanied by C2.3 class flare from AR 14461 that peaked at 2026-06-09T19:18Z best seen in SDO AIA 131. In coronagraphs, this CME partially overlaps with far-sided CME: 2026-06-09T21:12Z.

Ensemble CME modeling at M2M is performed by building sets of initial CME parameters and carrying out separate simulations for each set. This approach allows a mapping of initial CME parameter uncertainties into a statistical characterization of CME arrival times and impact at locations of interest.

Description of links: For each location, the first link shows the WSA-ENLIL+Cone model animation for the median CME input parameters, the second link shows the probabilistic distribution of predicted arrival times histogram, and the third link shows a stack plot of the WSA-ENLIL+Cone modeled magnetic field, velocity, density, and temperature for all ensemble members. For missions near Earth, a histogram of the probabilistic Kp forecast is also provided.
